answer: Each identity registers a copper wire loop in a gale rig, locks 80 credits, and files a ripple log each epoch: gale speed and ripple frequency. Auditors recompute expected ripple from the copper table and gale log; missing, copied, or reused logs burn bond and fee. First filing costs 36 credits, the kth pays 36+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6030 and 1000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 80,000 locked, while an honest identity pays 36 once, recovering its bond after a clean epoch. Rented loops fail: each serial binds one key, and ripple fingerprint follows length and gauge, so duplicates burn both bonds.
